items.text: Remember if you're having coffee with heavy cream, you ARE having breakfast!  It's not as much as eggs with bacon, but it's calories.  You can always try to nibble on a few nuts (careful with those - weigh your amounts!) throughout the morning if you're really concerned that you need to hit some sort of caloric target for the morning.
[Dried edamame!] (http://www.seapointfarms.com/products/dry-roasted-edamame.html)  3 net carbs for 13 grams of protein, so it's a nice punch of protein in perfect snack form.

You're right at the point that a LOT of people pause in their weight loss.  Your body is working hard right now on fat adaptation - give yourself some time and you'll be back to losing weight soon!  (PROVIDED that you're at a caloric deficit, of course, so if you're not tracking and weighing your food, get serious about that!)
How much magnesium are you getting?  When are your cramps worse?  Have you tried taking the magnesium a few hours before bed?

So, I'm going to challenge you to take things a step further and invest in yourself and your health more.  You've likely heard these instructions if you've ever flown on a plane: "Put on your own oxygen mask before assisting others." 

You're already packing your lunch.  Now, mealprep your dinners too.  When the little one is down for a nap or bed on the weekends, whip up some dinners for the week that you can prepackage that require minimal prep the day off.  Or, sit down and meal plan so that at 4pm you know exactly what you're making and it's just tossing it together, perhaps even pre-portioned even if it's not cooked.  

You've said it yourself - the energy from keto will come if you stick with it.  The stress of work and parenting is easier when you're not feeling so tired and when you're making progress on your weight loss.

You're worth the investment.

My spouse feels the same way about keto - he lost the weight he wanted to lose, and has stayed keto in maintaining his weight but he never had the "Wow, this is AMAZING" feeling that keto brings me.  He's obviously happy with his weight, happy that he doesn't get as hungry if he's a bit late for a meal, and enjoys his meals, but it's absolutely nothing extreme.

How often do I:  Used to be daily, now it's whenever.  Every few days-ish?

How often should you:  That's an entirely separate question.  Does hopping on the scale motivate you?  Help you commit to a day of keto eating?  Help you monitor your progress?  Or does it make you panic you when you see the absolutely normal ups and downs that successful weight loss means day to day?  Does it upset you that it's not "fast enough" or that you feel like your goal weight is just too far away?

Basically, my advice - weigh yourself as often as it's helpful to YOU, and not more.

Protein shakes are a pretty important way for me to hit my own protein macro, so I'm not going to discourage you!  I would urge you to really pack in the vitamins and minerals, though, for your dinner, and think about meal prepping breakfasts as those truly are super easy.  My spouse would make [these, swapping in and out a few ingregients](https://www.dietdoctor.com/recipes/keto-egg-muffins) on the weekend and take a couple to work each day.

Vegan ketoer here, and lemme tell you, my salads with a nice full-fat dressing are AMAZING.  :)

But it's absolutely true that keto when you're on a limited diet (vegan or vegetarian, or with various allergies) takes more homework to vary the meal options while hitting your protein macro.  Check out the other subs for recipes, but in all honesty, you can still eat similar to pre-keto if you sub in low carb options.  Miss black beans?  Look up black soy beans.  You can still have peanut butter - just look for ones that are sugar free.  If you eat cheese, you can turn cheese into crackers in the microwave.

My spouse is in maintenance - he hit his goal weight (which was pretty arbitrary), and as we were upping his caloric amounts to find his maintenance sweet spot (and because he was just so used to eating at a deficit) he kept losing as we were tweaking.  His weight has stabilized and he's 6lbs lower than his goal, and he's happy there.  Could he go lower?  Eh, yeah?  Does he need to?  Not for his peace of mind, and not according to the BMI chart.  

I'm getting closer to my first goal weight and will also be soon setting my next goal.  I'm going to start with 154 (which is the normal BMI for 5'6") and then see how I'm doing/feeling.  Like you, the idea of being at the bottom of the normal BMI range?  freaking UNTHINKABLE!
I feel rude saying this, but you look like your own daughter!  Absolutely incredible!

[This is what I eat](https://julianbakery.com/product/pegan-protein-bar-vanilla-cinnamon-twist/).  When you read reviews on like amazon, though, you'll see that 25% of people apparently loathe them.  I've had 2 boxes so far and each bar has been soft and, if not amazing in taste, it's not bad either.  Net carbs aren't too bad, and it's got a lot of protein.

When I started keto I'd use coconut oil in a BPC every morning (just regular, not MTC) but as keto decreased my hunger so much, I phased that out to just black coffee and now only use coconut oil when I need a fat bomb to bring up my calories.
I've only seen them online, and I buy them through Amazon.

[This is what I use](https://www.nowfoods.com/sports-nutrition/pea-protein-pure-unflavored-powder).  Is it tasty?  Nope.  But it gets the job done.  You can doctor it up as you wish, but I usually just chug it with unsweetened almond milk.

However, as other responses make clear - you can absolutely have protein powders that are whey based without spiking your insulin.  Just read the labels for net carb info.

Lots of folks pause where you are right now, don't panic.  However, I'd suggest you re-calculate your macros if you haven't so that when your body finishes up fat adaption you'll get right back to losing (although, unfortunately, at not the same pace)
Welcome to the family!  Don't hesitate to reach out if you have questions!

I only know how to do it this way:

Using a proper browser (not a phone app) visit the sub at /r/keto. In the top right of the screen, there is a control that reads "Show my flair on this reddit. It looks like:". Check this and click edit to enter whatever you want.
This is the part about keto that I find is harder than anything else for non-keto folks to grasp.  I get so many blank looks when I talk about this.

Great progress in those 2 weeks!

And, you know, I've still not had that nightmare. (looks around for wood to knock on...)

Here's the deal - popcorn, grains, fruits were all things I loved too.  My go-to items.  But I said to myself that I didn't want to keep feeling the way I did.  I was willing to give vegan keto a chance at 100% effort for 2 weeks to see what happened.

Literally one of the best decisions of my life.  Within days I felt like a new person.  Cravings and constant hunger? Gone.  I didn't need go-to items because I wasn't using food as comfort anymore.  Food is fuel.  I eat a small meal at 2pm and and dinner about 5:30pm, fasting the other 20 hours.  (OMAD is really tough for me - I usually feel pretty miserably full after so try to break it up into to meals)  I've been vegan keto since mid-June 2018.

Do I miss fruit?  Nope.  A few raspberries are such a flavor explosion that I can have a few grams of them and feel quite content.  (Yes, I weight my food in grams.  I'm also using keto for weight loss so close tracking is critical for me.)

What's included and excluded in keto?  I see that question a lot, and the answer is, if it fits your macros, it's keto.  My net carb limit is 20g - it's restrictive, but I'm fine with that.  However, as mentioned by /u/pandas_dont_poop a lot of vegans go higher in their net carb limit to give themselves more options.  Anyhoo, set your limit and start playing around with meal planning.  I, too, use Cronometer, and what finally got me to take the plunge with keto was sitting down with Cronometer and planning out a few days of meals to see what fit my macros wile ensuring I get enough protein.  

Plan a few days of meals, read up on electrolytes and be prepared to supplement them from day one, and then jump.  2 weeks is an incredibly short time to try something at 100% effort.

Where did you get an estimate of 40% body fat?  That seems pretty high for you given your stats.

Next, I'd consider using a keto calculator [such as this one](https://keto-calculator.ankerl.com/) - to configure your macros a bit different.  Your net carb limit can be set at 20 grams, you don't need to adhere to percentages with keto unless you're on a special keto regimen to manage certain conditions.  When it comes to estimating your exercise, for weight loss it's recommended that you actually keep your activity at sedentary in the calculator, and then set your caloric limit.  I think you'll find your caloric target will be a bit lower than you currently have now.  I threw some numbers together, but I recommend that you play around yourself:

---
*Generated by [Keto Calculator](https://keto-calculator.ankerl.com) 9.13*

27/F/5'5" | CW 138 | 30% BF | Mostly sedentary

* 1198 kcal Goal, a 20% deficit. (658 min, 1498 max)
* 20g Carbohydrates
* 77g Protein (58g min, 96g max)
* 90g Fat (30g min, 123g max)

----

27/M/5'5" | CW 138 | 30% BF | Mostly sedentary

* 1344 kcal Goal, a 20% deficit. (658 min, 1680 max)
* 20g Carbohydrates
* 77g Protein (58g min, 96g max)
* 106g Fat (30g min, 143g max)

----

Now, to answer your question about OMAD and fasting?  Go for it.  Not only will it not negatively impact your keto diet, but you may find that you prefer to only have one meal a day or fast regularly as your hunger decreases on keto.  Your priority, though, is to hit your protein target when you do eat to preserve your muscle mass.

Basically, since you want to lose weight, you need to eat at a caloric deficit.  From your screenshot, your caloric target is 1470, but from these rough calculations above, that's not eating at much of a deficit.  Eating keto alone won't cause much weight loss - you still need to eat fewer calories.

For me, it became the new normal.  But at the same time, I still have times where I realize that I'm feeling so much better than I was pre-keto, that I'm managing stress better, and that I'm accomplishing more that before.
You're in the 3-4 week pause that's SUPER common for people starting out.  Just keep calm and keto on, and the weight loss will restart (provided you're staying at a caloric deficit!)

Hello,

Glad you you're seeing the appetite suppression in keto - makes a caloric deficit a LOT easier to hit!

Your post doesn't give us a whole lot to go on, though.  What are your stats?  What are your current macros?  How are you tracking your intake?

Obligatory reminder to [read the FAQ](https://www.reddit.com/r/keto/wiki/faq) - it's absolutely packed with key info.

You asked for resources, so I'm going to throw a few at you:

[Main keto sub FAQ](https://www.reddit.com/r/keto/wiki/faq) - Just ignore references to bacon.  :)  Good content about how keto works overall.

I prefer the simplest calculator possible, [but people swear by this one](https://keto-calculator.ankerl.com/) for macro calculations.  As you've seen from other posters, many vegans shoot for closer to 30g for their net carb limit.  I stick with 20g.

[A nice vegetable guide for keto](https://www.ruled.me/best-low-carb-vegetables-ketogenic-diet/) I go back to this website occasionally 10 months later still for a quick reference to spur some more recipe ideas.

One thing to keep in mind is the part about keto that feels like freaking magic: you will (hopefully!) see very quickly that you don't need the large volume of veggies that you would rely on to feel full/satisfied.  Being in a caloric deficit for weight loss is so much easier than the constant struggle of CICO when you're not walking around always hungry. When you're hitting your protein macro reliably, you'll feel better overall too... if you are a vegan like me who never truly was getting enough protein and didn't realize it prior to keto.

Glad to hear you're already off to a solid start!  On those electrolytes - an electrolyte water off the shelf won't be enough.  Look at making your own ketoade.  My recipe:

*     1 teaspoon lemon juice
*     1 teaspoon lime juice
*     1/2 teaspoon Morton regular salt (1,180mg sodium)
*     1/4 teaspoon Morton lite salt (278.5mg sodium, 354.2mg potassium)
*     22oz water

I try to sip that throughout the day. I add more salt or lite salt based on my intake of sodium and potassium from food per my mealplan for the day. If it's too strong, add more water. If it's not enough, have a second batch later in the day.  I buy the lemon and lime juice in bottles from the market, because I don't have the time nor patience to squeeze my own!

For magnesium, I take 200mg of Magnesium Citrate a few hours before bed to combat restless/aching legs.
Outstanding weight loss and even better mental game going on!  Congrats on both.
I don't find the "hi, I'm new here" posts annoying - what I find annoying is getting to "meet" people and have them not keep us updated!  Keep us posted on your progress.  You've got this.

You know the mantra - KCKO.

I also had a pause on the scale for about a month before things got back into gear and I started losing consistently again.  Your pause, too, will pass.  Skip a Sunday weigh-in if it's causing you grief and just focus on how you feel.

Try to be more specific here about what kept derailing you.  Did you find yourself hungry and stressed and therefore reaching for an easy meal with carbs?  Is your pantry filled with things that really don't NEED to be in there?  Did you find yourself succumbing to non-keto meals when out with friends/family?  Basically - get out your thinking cap and truly assess what are your triggers, and then commit to changing things so that being keto is easier.

* Meal prep/plan.  I know what I'm eating for the day before I eat **anything** that day.
* Clear out junk.  Hard to do when you live with or cook for others, but even if that means putting it in a different cupboard or a higher shelf, make reaching for it something that takes more effort so that you have more time to tell yourself, "stop - why am I choosing food over my mental and physical health?!"
* Don't socialize hungry.  Fun times with friends/family may involve food, but they don't have to REVOLVE around food.  Have a solid meal or snack before you go out so that when you're out you can have something light (or just sip a beverage) and focus on the people, not the food.

Don't think about staying committed to keto.  Commit to yourself.

I, also, lost a lot of weight with CICO in my normal diet and it was such a STRUGGLE to talk myself into re-starting when I'd fall off the wagon.  That's the beauty of keto.  You are still at a caloric deficit for weight loss, but for me it's not at all the day-to-day struggle that CICO was.  I hope you experience the same!

[Here's my go-to guide on veggies](https://www.ruled.me/best-low-carb-vegetables-ketogenic-diet/).   Basically - carrots aren't your best choice per se, but if it's gotta be carrots, then you just need to plan the rest of your day carefully.  I strongly recommend that you explore trackers such as MyFitnessPal or Cronometer (my preference) and do some meal planning. Basically - plug in your preferred foods, see how those fit into your calculated macros, and then explore substitutions to stay within your net carb limit.

1. You're still in the honeymoon of keto, so even ovulation can't completely stop the water weight loss.  I'm afraid that for a lot of women, next month you won't see the same steady progress down, but more of a pause or slight uptick and then weight loss a bit later. 
2. Electrolytes!  [Read the FAQ](https://www.reddit.com/r/keto/wiki/faq#wiki_how_do_i_replenish_electrolytes_when_i_am_deficient.3F), and seriously - supplement.  No really, do it.  Yes, I promise.  No, salting your food isn't enough.  For me, 200mg of magnesium citrate a few hours before bed made my cramping and restless leg symptoms vanish.
3. In the first 2 weeks, it's mostly water weight.  Is that trivial or stupid?  Hell no.  It's weight you're not carrying around!  It's weight not putting stress on your body/joints.  Woo!  And is this too good to be true?  Ehh, look around at the flairs on the sub.  I think you'll see that for a lot of us, we'll take this too good to be true and run with it!

Keep us posted on your progress!
